title: MASTER_KEY is stretched into the AES-256-GCM content key by a single unsalted SHA-256 round with no entropy floor anywhere in the config path — the at-rest protection of providers.api_key_enc degrades entirely to the guessing entropy of one env var (downgraded from high: medium)
evidence: Verified verbatim, exact line anchors, by reading each cited file end-to-end. crypto.go:21-23: `func NewCipher(masterKey string) (*Cipher, error) {` / `sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(masterKey))` / `block, err := aes.NewCipher(sum[:])` (line 22 is the SHA-256 derivation itself, so the filed anchor is correct). config.go:64: `MasterKey:          getenv("MASTER_KEY", "llm-router-guard-master-key"),` and getenv (config.go:30-35) `if v := os.Getenv(k); v != "" { return v }` — no normalization, no length check. Single producer/consumer confirmed by grep of `MasterKey`: config.go:17, config.go:64, main.go:50 `enc, err := crypto.NewCipher(cfg.MasterKey)`. No entropy check exists at any layer; aes.NewCipher can never reject a weak key because the digest is always 32 bytes, so the `if err != nil` branch at crypto.go:24-26 is dead for input-quality purposes. Sealing is concentrated on one column: providers.go:64 `enc, err := s.enc.Encrypt(req.APIKey)` (and :112 for updates) -> providers.api_key_enc, model.go:107; decryption at providers.go:163 `key, _ := s.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc)`, health.go:121, manager.go:214 `if plain, err := m.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc); err == nil {`. Warning is a case-sensitive single-literal equality test: main.go:191 `if cfg.MasterKey == "llm-router-guard-master-key" {` -> main.go:192 WARNING, non-blocking.
impact: Confirmed but scoped narrower than filed. What is true: the content key is one SHA-256 round away from an operator-chosen passphrase, there is no minimum-entropy floor, GCM's auth tag (crypto.go:52) gives the cracker a zero-false-positive verification oracle at ~1 hash + 1 AES-open per candidate, one key decrypts the whole providers table, and no code path lets MASTER_KEY actually be rotated (no re-seal routine exists in internal/admin; main.go:192 and help.ts:51 tell operators every provider key must be re-entered). What bounds it: the input to the cracking job — providers.api_key_enc — is unreachable through the application. Both APIKeyEnc and the in-memory plaintext APIKey are `json:"-"` (model.go:107-108), so listProviders (providers.go:44), create/update responses (which blank the field at :81/:130), /config/export (configstatus.go:68) and /backups/:id/download (backup.go:53) never emit ciphertext or plaintext; ConfigBundle (bundle.go:17) and audit.LogOp (audit.go:114 json.Marshal) likewise drop it, so the operator's own backup artifacts contain no crackable material; and there is no online oracle — Decrypt is only called on stored rows with errors swallowed (providers.go:163, health.go:122-124, manager.go:218). The exploit therefore needs two independent, out-of-band conditions: a storage-layer leak of the DB (SQLite file, MySQL/PG dump, replica or snapshot) AND a low-entropy MASTER_KEY. In the default single-node topology the breach that yields the DB file also yields the environment/.env, where the attacker reads the key instead of cracking it. Real residual impact = every upstream provider billing key in the DB-only-leak case, which is exactly the scenario at-rest encryption exists for.
mitigations_checked: AES-GCM usage is correct and NOT part of the defect: fresh 12-byte nonce from crypto/rand per Encrypt (crypto.go:35-36), nonce prepended at :39 `ct := c.aead.Seal(nonce, nonce, []byte(plain), nil)`, tag enforced at :52; reuse is a birthday-bound event, not a volume heuristic. Ciphertext (not plaintext) is what is stored; plaintext is never persisted. api_key_enc is `json:"-"` so it is absent from every API response, export, backup and operation log. Gateway API keys are SHA-256 (apikeys.go:40), admin passwords bcrypt (main.go:175), TOTP recovery codes hashed — none derive from MASTER_KEY, so blast radius is one column. JWT_SECRET is a separate secret, so this weakness grants no authentication bypass. No AAD binding to provider ID (additionalData nil at :39/:52) — code-true, but impact-free: an attacker with DB write access can insert their own provider row or repoint an alias and capture keys live, so no crypto is needed. Documents actively warn (though nothing enforces): .env.template:3 `cp .env.template .env && 编辑 .env`, :19 `生产环境必须替换！`, README.md:143 `MASTER_KEY="your-strong-secret"`, quickstart.md:52/90, help.ts:47/51. Case-mismatched compose fallback docker-compose.yml:16 `- MASTER_KEY=${MASTER_KEY:-CHANGE-ME-MASTER-KEY}` never equals main.go:191's literal so no warning prints — genuine aggravator, but already carried by verify-authn-1-2 and not double-counted here. Additional exposure the original auditor missed: api_key_masked (crypto.go:65 `return string(r[:4]) + "****" + string(r[len(r)-2:])`) ships a known prefix/suffix and exact plaintext length per row in every listing/export/backup, marginally accelerating candidate verification.
corrections_to_filed_writeup: 'unsalted' is the wrong axis: with a single global master key mandated identical across all instances (README.md:263), a per-record salt buys nothing against an offline dictionary attack on that secret; the missing property is iteration/memory-hardness. The recommended 'random salt in the ciphertext header' also implies a storage-format change plus per-instance salt provenance the finding does not address.

'the code and .env.template encourage copy-paste of the shipped default' is overstated — template line 3 instructs editing, line 19 says replacement is mandatory, README/quickstart/UI help all repeat it; only enforcement is missing.
'no AAD binding (rows could be swapped)' adds no severity: a DB-write-capable attacker already holds strictly more power than this weakness grants.
'every provider API key' is the full and only scope of the cipher, so 'bulk decrypt' should not be read as a broader key-compromise.
recommendation: Run the derivation through a memory-hard KDF once at startup — Argon2id (x/crypto/argon2 already reachable via the bcrypt dependency set) or scrypt — since it is per-process, not per-message, so cost is irrelevant at this call volume; keep AES-256-GCM. Prepend a version/format byte plus the KDF salt/parameters to the stored blob so the change is lazily migratable, and ship the missing re-encrypt tooling (iterate providers, Decrypt with the old cipher, Encrypt with the new, save) so the startup text at main.go:192 stops telling operators rotation means manual re-entry. Enforce a floor at config.Load or NewCipher (reject empty and <32 chars / non-random master keys, and refuse to boot in gin.ReleaseMode rather than only logging), make warnInsecureDefaults case-insensitive and set-based so `CHANGE-ME-MASTER-KEY` (docker-compose.yml:16) also trips it, and additionally bind provider identity as AAD in Seal/Open so rows cannot be transplanted. If MASTER_KEY is meant to hold only single-host value, document that co-located .env + gateway.db provides no real separation and steer multi-node deployments to an external KMS/secret manager delivering a 256-bit random value.
